core_obligations: Note that the proof is that of the radical-element lemma with the higher-dimensional lemmas substituted, and record why the catenary hypothesis is what licenses the substitution: every height one prime has dimension d - 1, so Spec(R/(f + h)) is equidimensional (proof lines 38399-38409).

For each height one prime p containing f, use that R_p is a discrete valuation ring, record the valuations ord_p(f), and define div(f) = sum_j m_j q_j over the distinct height one primes q_j containing f (proof lines 38412-38426).

Observe that R/fR is reduced exactly when m_j = 1 for all j, using that q_1, ..., q_s are the associated primes of R/fR and that R/fR embeds into the product of its localizations at them (proof lines 38427-38434).
Choose g_2, ..., g_{d-1} and N as in the height-one-polynomial lemma, define t(y) as the number of primes minimal over y, and note t(f) = s (proof lines 38437-38445).

Using the catenary property and the height-one-polynomial lemma, prove the chain of equalities bounding t(f + h) above by the length of R/(f, g_1, ..., g_{d-1}) for h in m^N, so that t(f + h) is bounded independently of h (proof lines 38446-38459).
Pick h in m^N cap J maximizing t(f + h), replace f by f + h, and conclude that t(f + h) <= s for every h in m^N cap J (proof lines 38462-38467).

Show that any h in m^N cap J with ord_{q_j}(h) >= 1 and ord_{q_j}(h) = 1 exactly when m_j > 1 yields ord_{q_j}(f + h) = 1 for all j, so that div(f + h) has the q_j with coefficient one plus extra primes, and hence by v = 0 supplies the desired element (proof lines 38470-38483).

Construct such an h: use prime avoidance to choose a_j in q_j cap J avoiding the other q_{j'}, choose b_j in J cap q_1 cap ... cap q_s outside the second symbolic power q_j^{(2)} (legitimate because the radical ideal J' = J cap q_1 cap ... cap q_s has reduced quotient at each q_j), form c = sum_j b_j prod_{j' not j} a_{j'} with ord_{q_j}(c) = 1 for all j, and set h = c prod_{m_j = 1} a_j y for suitable y in m^N avoiding all q_j (proof lines 38486-38512).
difficulty_reason: The proposition takes a catenary Noetherian local normal domain R of dimension d and a radical ideal J, and asserts the existence of a nonzero f in J with R/fR reduced (source lines 38386-38396). The proof spells out in full what the shorter radical-element lemma does, and the catenary hypothesis is used essentially: it makes every height one prime have dimension d - 1, so that the spectrum of R/(f + h) is equidimensional and the height-one-polynomial lemma applies (proof lines 38405-38409). The proof then sets up the divisor div(f) = sum m_j q_j over the height one primes containing f, observes that R/fR is reduced exactly when all m_j equal 1, and uses that R/fR embeds into the product of its localizations at those primes (proof lines 38414-38434). It introduces t(y) as the number of minimal primes over y and, using the catenary property together with the height-one-polynomial lemma, bounds t(f + h) independently of h in the power m^N (proof lines 38437-38459). Maximality of t over h in m^N cap J is then used to replace f so that t(f + h) <= s for all such h (proof lines 38462-38467), after which the desired h is manufactured: elements a_j in q_j cap J avoiding the other q_j' and elements b_j in J cap q_1 cap ... cap q_s outside the second symbolic power q_j^{(2)}, combined into c = sum b_j prod a_j', then multiplied by the a_j with m_j = 1 and by a suitable y (proof lines 38470-38512). The non-routine content is the boundedness of t, which is what makes the maximality argument possible, and the prime-avoidance construction of c with prescribed valuations.
